title: “Monks, these six sense bases — well-guarded, well-protected, well-guarded, well-restrained — bring happiness. What six? The eye sense base, monks — well-guarded, well-protected, well-guarded, well-restrained…
content: “Monks, these six sense bases — well-guarded, well-protected, well-guarded, well-restrained — bring happiness. What six? The eye sense base, monks — well-guarded, well-protected, well-guarded, well-restrained — brings happiness. The ear … The nose … The tongue … The body … The mind sense base, monks — well-guarded, well-protected, well-guarded, well-restrained — brings happiness. These six sense bases, monks — well-guarded, well-protected, well-guarded, well-restrained — bring happiness.”

title: Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa recited this verse to the Venerable Ānanda: Sensual desire burns me, My mind is on fire. It is good, O disciple…
content:
Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa recited this verse to the Venerable Ānanda:
Sensual desire burns me,
My mind is on fire.
It is good, O disciple of Gotama,
Out of compassion,
Teach me the Dhamma to extinguish the blaze.

(Ānanda):
It is because of distorted perception
That your mind is on fire.
Abandon the sign of the beautiful
That is connected with sensual desire.
See formations as impermanent,
Suffering, and not-self —
Extinguish great sensual desire,
Do not be burned again and again.
Develop the mind on foulness,
Unified, well-concentrated,
Practice mindfulness of the body,
Develop much disenchantment.
Practice the signless,
Destroy the underlying tendency to conceit,
And by thoroughly penetrating conceit,
Your practice will be at peace.

title: - “Venerable Kaccāna, ‘guarding the sense faculties, guarding the sense faculties’ is said. To what extent, Venerable Kaccāna, is there guarding of the sense faculties?”…
content: - “Venerable Kaccāna, ‘guarding the sense faculties, guarding the sense faculties’ is said. To what extent, Venerable Kaccāna, is there guarding of the sense faculties?” - “Here, brahmin, when a person sees a form with the eye, his mind inclines toward agreeable forms and recoils from disagreeable forms. He dwells with mindfulness unestablished, with a limited mind. He does not know as it actually is the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom. Therefore, evil, unwholesome states that have arisen are not abandoned without remainder. When he hears a sound … smells an odor … tastes a flavor … feels a touch … cognizes a phenomenon with the mind, his mind inclines toward agreeable phenomena and recoils from disagreeable phenomena. He dwells with mindfulness unestablished, with a limited mind. He does not know as it actually is the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom. Therefore, evil, unwholesome states that have arisen are not abandoned without remainder. Thus, brahmin, there is non-guarding of the sense faculties.”

title: Elder Nun Selā: You will not escape, You will not escape this world. What use is this practice of seclusion to you? Enjoy sensual pleasures…
content:
Elder Nun Selā:

You will not escape,
You will not escape this world.
What use is this practice of seclusion to you?
Enjoy sensual pleasures —
Do not have regrets later.

Sensual pleasures are like swords and spears —
They cut the aggregates to pieces.
What you call the pleasure of life —
For me, that sensual pleasure
Is no longer enticing.

Everywhere, delight is destroyed.
The mass of darkness,
The blinding darkness, has been shattered.
Know this, O Evil One —
You are Māra,
You are defeated.

title: “Furthermore, monks, one sees that woman’s corpse thrown in a charnel ground — eaten by crows, or by hawks, or by vultures, or by dogs,…
content: “Furthermore, monks, one sees that woman’s corpse thrown in a charnel ground — eaten by crows, or by hawks, or by vultures, or by dogs, or by jackals, or by various worms. What do you think, monks? Has her former charm and beauty disappeared and peril become evident?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Thus, monks, is the peril in the case of forms.”

title: - “How, venerable sir, should one know, how should one see, so that ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises?” - “Monk, knowing and seeing…
content: - “How, venerable sir, should one know, how should one see, so that ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises?” - “Monk, knowing and seeing the eye as impermanent, ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises. Knowing and seeing forms as impermanent … eye-consciousness … eye-contact … Whatever feeling arises dependent on eye-contact … knowing and seeing that feeling as impermanent, ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises. The ear … The nose … The tongue … The body … Knowing and seeing the mind as impermanent, ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises. Phenomena … mind-consciousness … mind-contact … Whatever feeling arises dependent on mind-contact … knowing and seeing that feeling as impermanent, ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises. Knowing thus, seeing thus, monks, ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises.”

title: “Monks, it is because of not realizing, not penetrating the Four Noble Truths that you and I have wandered and wandered through this long course.…
content:
“Monks, it is because of not realizing, not penetrating the Four Noble Truths that you and I have wandered and wandered through this long course. What four? Because of not realizing, not penetrating the noble truth of suffering, monks, you and I have wandered and wandered through this long course … the noble truth of the origin of suffering … the noble truth of the cessation of suffering … Because of not realizing, not penetrating the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering, monks, you and I have wandered and wandered through this long course. But now, monks, the noble truth of suffering has been realized and penetrated. The noble truth of the origin of suffering has been realized and penetrated. The noble truth of the cessation of suffering has been realized and penetrated. The noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering has been realized and penetrated. Cut off is craving for existence; destroyed is what leads to renewed existence. Now there is no further becoming.” The Blessed One said this … the Teacher further said:

From not seeing the four noble truths
As they really are,
One wanders for a long time
Through many births.
But when these are seen,
The root of rebirth is pulled out,
The root of suffering is cut off —
Now there is no further becoming.

title: “Monk, I say that there are these three feelings: pleasant feeling, painful feeling, neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. These three feelings have been spoken of by me. But,…
content: “Monk, I say that there are these three feelings: pleasant feeling, painful feeling, neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. These three feelings have been spoken of by me. But, monk, I also say: ‘Whatever is felt is included in suffering.’ It is in relation to the impermanence of formations that this is said: ‘Whatever is felt is included in suffering.’ It is in relation to the nature of destruction, the nature of vanishing, the nature of fading away, the nature of cessation, the nature of change of formations that this is said: ‘Whatever is felt is included in suffering.’”

title: “Monks, just as in the autumn, when the sky is clear and free of clouds, the sun, rising in the sky, dispels all darkness from…
content: “Monks, just as in the autumn, when the sky is clear and free of clouds, the sun, rising in the sky, dispels all darkness from space, shines, glows, and blazes — so too, by developing and cultivating the perception of impermanence, all lust for sensual pleasures is abandoned, all lust for form is abandoned, all lust for existence is abandoned, all ignorance is abandoned, all conceit ‘I am’ is abandoned. And how, monks, is the perception of impermanence developed and cultivated so that … all conceit ‘I am’ is abandoned? ‘This is form, this is the arising of form, this is the cessation of form. This is feeling … this is perception … these are formations … this is consciousness, this is the arising of consciousness, this is the cessation of consciousness.’ It is when the perception of impermanence is developed and cultivated in this way, monks, that all lust for sensual pleasures is abandoned … all conceit ‘I am’ is abandoned.”

title: “Like a pit of filth Accumulated for many years — So too, a defiled person Is very hard to cleanse. Monks, know such a person…
content:
“Like a pit of filth
Accumulated for many years —
So too, a defiled person
Is very hard to cleanse.

Monks, know such a person —
Attached to households,
With evil desires, evil intentions,
Evil conduct, evil practices.

All of you, being of one mind,
Should shun such a person.
Blow him away like dust,
Throw him out like rubbish.

Expel the verbose one,
The fake ascetic.
Having expelled evil desires,
Evil conduct, evil practices —

Keep yourselves pure,
Live with the pure,
Mindful, dwelling together,
Wise, and make an end of suffering.”
